references.text: Also mentions Zion (Hermon) as part of the conquered area east of the Jordan, confirming Hermon's alternative name.
Describes the same geographical area from the Arnon to Mount Hermon that Israel conquered.
Mentions Mount Hermon in connection with the borders of the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites.
Mentions Sirion (Hermon) in a poetic description where the Lord's voice makes Lebanon and Sirion leap like a calf.
Mentions Hermon in connection with the dew that falls on the mountains of Zion, an image of blessing and unity.
Mentions Senir and Hermon as mountains in the north, confirming that Senir is another name for Hermon.
Describes Israel's conquest of the land from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Hermon.
Mentions that planks were made of cypress trees from Senir, confirming that Senir was known for its timber.
Describes Israel's conquest of the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, which is the background for the mention of the Amorites in the verse.
